THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
Though matter is listed for admission, with consent of learned counsel for parties, it is taken-up for final disposal.

2. Challenging judgment and award dated 29.06.2018 passed by Senior Civil Judge and MACT,
Chincholi (for short, 'Tribunal') in M.V.C.no.210/2016, this appeal is filed.
3. Shri Sanjeevkumar C.Patil, learned counsel for appellant submitted that appeal was by claimant seeking for enhancement of compensation.

It was submitted that before Tribunal, finding were recorded about occurrence of accident, involving of insured vehicle due to rash and negligent driving by its driver, sufferance of disability by claimant, coverage of insurance as on date of accident and NC: 2023:KHC-K:6424 liability of insurer to pay compensation.
Since insurer had not preferred appeal against said award, they had attained finality.

4. Insofar as enhancement, it was submitted that as on date of accident i.e., 07.11.2015, claimant was 35 years old coolie earning `12,000/- per month who sustained fracture of lateral condoyle of right patella, head of tibia and fibula of right leg, assessed by PW.2 - Dr.Ravi Eshwarappa to have caused 33% disability to limb.
However, Tribunal considered meager extent of loss of earning capacity at 10%.
It was further submitted that Tribunal had assessed inadequate monthly income at `6,000/-.
Therefore, compensation under head of future of loss of income required enhancement.
5. It was submitted that for several grievous fractures sustained, award of `20,000/- towards pain and suffering was inadequate.

Likewise, claimant sought enhancement of compensation under loss Baimulla Narsimula vs Mohamamd Shafiqshaik And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191951524/
2 of amenities, NC: 2023:KHC-K:6424 towards attendant and other incidental charges and loss of income during laid-up period.

sentences.text: 6. On other hand, Shri Subhash Mallapur learned counsel for respondent no.2/Insurer sought to support award and oppose enhancement.
7. Heard learned counsel.
Perused impugned judgment and award.

8. From above submission, since insurer has not preferred appeal and only claimant is in appeal for enhancement, the point that would arise for consideration is 'whether claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as sough for ?"
9.
Though claimant has stated that his monthly earning was `12,000/- from coolie work, same is not substantiated with evidence.
In absence, notional income has to be considered.
Notional income for year 2015, adopted for purpose of settlement of cases before Lok- Adalat is `8,000/-.

Therefore,
same has to be considered.
Insofar as disability, claimant relied upon wound certificate, disability certificate and discharge summary marked as Ex.P.6, Ex.P.7 and Ex.P.10 respectively.
Based on said documents, PW.2 after clinical examination assessed limb disability to an extent of 33%.
It is seen that claimant is coolie by profession.
Injuries sustained are in the same region i.e., right knee.
The fractures sustained are virtually to all bones of right leg.
Therefore, disability/loss of earning capacity would be more severe.
Under such circumstances, assessment of functional disability at 10% by Tribunal would not be justified, it would be appropriate to consider it at 15%.

Thus, future loss of income would be:
`8,000/- X 15% X 12 X 16 = `2,30,400/-.
11.
Tribunal has awarded compensation of `73,407/- towards complete reimbursement of medical bills.
Therefore, same is sustained.
For several grievous fractures sustained, Tribunal has awarded meager amount of `20,000/- towards pain and suffering.
It would be NC: 2023:KHC-K:6424 appropriate to enhance it `50,000/- which would be just and proper.

Towards loss of amenities,
Tribunal has granted mere `10,000/-.
In view of above mentioned circumstances, it would be appropriate to enhance it to `25,000/-.

Normally fractures take about three months to heal,
considering same as period of lay off, claimant would be entitled compensation of `24,000/-
(8000x3) towards loss of income during laid-up period.

That apart, he would be entitled to `4,500/-
awarded by Tribunal towards incidental charges.
Thus claimant would be entitled for total compensation of `4,07,307/-.
Point for consideration is answered partly affirmative as above.

Consequently, following :
ORDER Appeal is allowed in part.

Compensation is enhanced from `2,35,100/- to `4,07,307/- which shall carry interest at rate of 6% per annum from date of petition Baimulla Narsimula vs Mohamamd Shafiqshaik And Anr on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/191951524/
3 till deposit.
